questions.question: Name the four layers of the atmosphere in order from the ground upwards, and state for each whether temperature increases or decreases with height.
questions.expected_answer: Troposphere: decreases. Stratosphere: increases. Mesosphere: decreases. Thermosphere: increases.

questions.question: Explain why the temperature in the troposphere decreases with height but the temperature in the stratosphere increases with height.
questions.expected_answer: The troposphere is heated mainly from below: sunlight warms the ground and oceans, which warm the air in contact with them, so the air is warmest near the surface and cools with height (about 6,5 °C per km). The stratosphere is heated from within/above by ozone absorbing ultraviolet radiation from the Sun; more UV is absorbed higher up, where sunlight arrives first, so the temperature rises with height.

questions.question: Explain why the ozone layer is important, and describe how human activities damaged it and what has been done about it.
questions.expected_answer: Ozone absorbs most of the Sun's harmful UV radiation, which would otherwise cause sunburn, skin cancer, cataracts and harm to plants and plankton. CFCs from fridges, air conditioners and aerosol sprays rose into the stratosphere and destroyed ozone, causing the ozone hole over Antarctica. The Montreal Protocol (1987), signed by South Africa and other countries, phased out CFCs, and the ozone layer is slowly recovering.
